title: Suona
summary: The suona is a double-reed horn of China with a conical wooden body, a brass mouth tube with a round lip disc, and a wide flaring brass bell. It is loud and bright, and a player can bend the notes into a wail or lift them into a fanfare.
howToPlay: A covered hole glows; an open hole shows its dark bore. Six notes of the five-note mode are lit down the tube.
Each strike shows the fingering of that note and the bell opens as it sounds.
Let the long notes ring before the next.
rules: A phrase is a line of notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It is played at weddings, festivals and village processions, where its piercing tone carries over drums and gongs.
